Warriors Would Be ‘First in Line’ For Devin Booker, Per Insider

Posted on September 13, 2026September 14, 2026 by Sam Pasfield
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:51
Instaread

Some interesting trade buzz surrounding Suns star Devin Booker has emerged – involving a Western Conference rival.

Booker is signed to a max contract extension with Phoenix that keeps him with the franchise through the 2029-30 season.

However, Golden State would be very interested if he was to ever become available in trade talks, Tim Kawakami recently revealed.

“I think the Warriors like him too much if you ask me. But they love him. Steve [Kerr] loves him,” he said on the Warriors Plus/Minus podcast.

“Booker loved playing for Steve. … They [Golden State] love Devin Booker. … Listen he obviously loves Phoenix, he’s signed long-term. They say they’re never trading him … But if that plays out in a poor way, they’ve traded every draft pick. How do they get draft picks back? How do they restart? I know the Warriors would be first in line saying, ‘we got three first round picks we can give you, and what else do you want?'”

Booker got to know Kerr and Steph Curry during Team USA’s Olympics campaign in Paris in 2024 and clearly they all got along very well.
Unless ownership at the Suns changes, the star guard appears to be very much staying put, so long as Mat Ishbia is around.

“Devin Booker is our franchise player,” Ishbia said at his end of season press conference.

“I love Devin Booker. Devin Booker loves being here. Our coach loves Devin Booker. Our GM loves Devin Booker. Devin Booker is going to be here. Devin Booker is going to lead us to a championship here in Phoenix. That’s what he’s going to do, and we’re going to build the right team around him.

“He’s going to get better, just like I’m going to get better, just like everyone is going to get better in our organization.”

In August, Ishbia had a hilarious response to a reporter asking him whether he’d ever trade D-Book to the Pistons.

“When I’m dead. Devin Booker will never be a Detroit Piston.”

So Warriors fans, you can keep dreaming.

Jaylen Brown Reveals What He Wants His Legacy to Be

Posted on September 13, 2026September 14, 2026 by KC Dean

Jaylen Brown has already put together a career most NBA players could only dream of, but the Sixers star doesn’t want basketball accomplishments to define his legacy.

Brown has five All-Star selections, two All-NBA honors, an Eastern Conference Finals MVP and a Finals MVP from his championship run with the Boston Celtics in 2024.

But when asked how he ultimately wants to be remembered, Brown made it clear his answer goes far beyond trophies and individual awards.

“I want to break down that fear. I’m not here for entertainment,” Brown said during an interview with two-time Oscar winner Mahershala Ali, according to Sixers Wire. “Like, God didn’t put me here to entertain some people. He gave me abilities to run, jump, speak, articulate myself, not for other people who don’t value me just to be entertained. I think my legacy will be, hopefully, is inspiring the next generation to be fearless.”

It’s a message that reflects how Brown has approached much of his career away from basketball.

The former No. 3 overall pick has regularly used his platform to discuss issues outside of the NBA, and his latest comments show that he views his influence beyond the court as an important part of what he will eventually leave behind.

Brown is now entering a completely different chapter of his basketball career with Philadelphia after spending his first 10 seasons with Boston.

His resume already ensures he will be remembered as one of the standout players of his generation, particularly after winning Finals MVP while helping the Celtics capture the 2024 NBA championship.

Now, Brown will have an opportunity to add to that resume with the Sixers.

Philadelphia hasn’t won an NBA championship since 1983, giving Brown and the Sixers the chance to end a title drought that has stretched more than four decades.

Another championship would only strengthen Brown’s basketball legacy.

But judging by his own words, when his career eventually comes to an end, Brown hopes what he inspired people to do will matter more than anything he accomplished on the court.
